strings: A flexible, superconducting insulated cable for heavy-duty power transfer.
A high-capacity superconducting magnetic energy storage (SMES) unit.
A pump for cycling an external airlock controlled by the connected doors.
A one meter section of regular pipe.
A heavy duty blast door that opens mechanically.
A flexible, superconducting insulated multilayer hub for heavy-duty multilayer power transfer.
It's coarse and rough and gets everywhere.
A lightweight support lattice. These hold our station together.
A flimsy framework of iron rods.
It's slippery and gooey. Perhaps it's the chef's cooking?
A square piece of iron standing on four metal legs. It can not move.
A first aid kit with the ability to heal common types of injuries.
Emergency air-tight shutter, capable of sealing off breached areas. This one has a glass panel. It has a mechanism to open it with just your hands.
A remotely-activatable dispenser for crowd-controlling foam.
Some type of shrubbery. Known for causing considerable economic stress on designers.
It's a floor-mounted device for projecting holographic images. This one will refuse to auto-connect incoming calls.
An outlet for the pneumatic disposal system.
A basin used to grow plants in.
A transit tube for moving things around.
A catwalk for easier EVA maneuvering and cable placement.
Now you see me, now you don't...
A machine that monitors atmosphere levels. Goes off if the area is dangerous.
A huge chunk of iron used to separate rooms.
A huge chunk of reinforced metal used to separate rooms.
A little bit of nature contained in a pot.
A large piece of space-resistant printed paper.
Heavy duty mechanical shutters with an atmospheric seal that keeps them airtight once closed.
A console used to interface with R&D tools.
Has a valve and pump attached to it.
A telescreen that connects to the minisat's camera network.
Pull this in case of emergency. Thus, keep pulling it forever.
The output side of a turbine generator, contains the turbine and the stator.
You can't tell if this is real grass or just cheap plastic imitation.
A sink used for washing one's hands and face. Passively reclaims water over time.
Different from the Middle Ages version.
By inserting components and a cell into this, wiring them up, and putting them into a shell, anyone can pretend to be a programmer.
It's seriously hampering your view of the jungle.
A control terminal for the area's electrical systems.
A sign labelling an area where the law is law.
A solar panel. Generates electricity when in contact with sunlight.
A standard metal table frame covered with an amazingly fancy, patterned cloth.

\"I'll sweeten thy sad grave: thou shalt not lack the flower that's like thy face, pale primrose, nor the azured hare-bell, like thy veins; no, nor the leaf of eglantine, whom not to slander, out-sweeten'd not thy breath.\"
A wall-mounted first aid station, designed to treat minor injuries - just stick your hand in and try to relax.
A heavy wooden box, which can be filled with a lot of ores or boulders
It's a secure locker for personnel. The first person to swipe their ID gains control.
A standard Nanotrasen-licensed newsfeed handler for use in commercial space stations. All the news you absolutely have no use for, in one place!
A reinforced version of the four legged table.
It's a normal black ink pen.
The cornerstone of any customer service job. You feel an unending urge to ring it.
A large vessel containing pressurized gas.
A sign with the Nanotrasen logo on it. Glory to Nanotrasen!
A lightbulb you can walk on without breaking it, amazing.
Used to seal minor hull breaches.
A window that is reinforced with metal rods.
Space Jesus, why didn't anyone clean this up? They smell terrible.
You sit in this. Either by will or force.
It's the hub of a teleporting machine.
A reprint of a poster from 2505, commemorating the 50th Anniversary of Nanoposters Manufacturing, a subsidiary of Nanotrasen.
HOLY SHEET! That is a lot of glass.
This space is blocked off by a crude assortment of planks.
Bluespace technologies on the application of bureaucracy.
Used for emergencies. Contains very little oxygen, so try to conserve it until you actually need it.
Spinward Sector Station SS-13 'Kilo' Class Outpost Commissioned 13/11/2559 Decommissioned Recommissioned 7/7/2566'Forever Different'
A pump that moves gas by pressure.
A portable item using blue-space technology. One of the buttons opens a portal, the other re-opens your last destination.
A covered turret that shoots at its enemies.
A special pipe to bridge pipe layers with.
A small screen which the AI can use to present itself.
Pstttthhh! Pass it under the table.
Instead of a license plate number, this could contain a quote like \"Live laugh love\".
Do not apply fire to this. Rumour says it burns easily.
Used to access the various cameras on the labor camp.
A trash bin, place your trash here for the janitor to collect.
Come on Lady Luck, spawn me a pair of sunglasses.
A bust depicting a certain 19th century economist. You get the feeling a specter is haunting the station.
From here you can research mysteries of the DNA!
Heavy duty, airtight, plastic flaps. Definitely can't get past those. No way.
A radio beacon used for bot navigation.
A warning sign which reads 'EXTERNAL AIRLOCK'.
A small wall mounted cabinet designed to hold a fire extinguisher.
Made by Space Amish using traditional space techniques, this heater/cooler is guaranteed not to set the station on fire. Warranty void if used in engines.
A trusty station intercom, ready to spring into action even when the headsets go silent.
A dish-shaped machine used to broadcast processed subspace signals.
A poster instructing the viewer to wear eye protection when dealing with chemicals, smoke, or bright lights.
A vending machine is guaranteed to spawn here, but its exact model is not known. The normal atlas view shows one possible outcome; the actual machine is chosen when the round starts.
A warning sign which reads 'NO SMOKING'.
A warning sign which reads 'ESCAPE PODS'.
It's a useless heap of junk... or is it?
Don't believe everything you see on a poster, patriots. All the lizards at central command don't want to answer this SIMPLE QUESTION: WHERE IS THE GAS MINER MINING FROM, CENTCOM?
The HT-451, a torque rotation-based, waste disposal unit for small matter. This one seems remarkably clean.
Mirror mirror on the wall, who's the most robust of them all?
A Prism-brand path illumination device. It is anchored in place and glowing steadily.
A one meter section of heat-exchanging pipe.
A warning sign which reads 'DANGER: FIRE'.
This device recharges energy-dependent lifeforms, like cyborgs, ethereals, and MODsuit users.
A one meter section of regular pipe used to connect pipenets over pipes.
A bacteriostatic mesh used to dress burns.
Basic sterile sutures used to seal up cuts and lacerations and stop bleeding.
Basic railing meant to protect idiots like you from falling.
The label indicates that it contains body bags.
A small, pistol-sized energy gun with a built-in flashlight. It has two settings: disable and kill.
Used to access the various cameras on the outpost.
A warning sign which reads 'SECURE AREA'.
A nasty looking shard of glass.
A board for pinning important notices upon. It is made of the finest Spanish cork.
A highly advanced vending machine for buying cargo related clothing for free.
Soft velvet carpeting. Feels good between your toes.
A small tool for digging and moving dirt.
It's used for removing weeds or scratching your back.
For connecting portables devices related to atmospherics control.
Used to order supplies, approve requests, and control the shuttle.
